## Natural history notes

A small pebble bee characterized by a compact black body with pale yellow to cream markings and the sturdy build typical of leafcutter-family bees. In Florida, the Florida Pebble Bee is recorded as Dianthidium floridiense and occurs in sunny open or semi-open habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, gardens, roadsides, and wildflower patches where nectar and pollen plants are available. Females collect pollen and nectar from flowers and, like other pebble bees, nest in small cavities or protected sites using resin, pebbles, or plant material to build or partition brood cells, making them solitary native pollinators rather than colony-forming bees.
